video_title: SHOCKING Offseason Moves! DeAndre Ayton Traded & LeBron Documentary Speculation?!

quotes.speaker: Wosny Lambre
quotes.summary_phrase: The lack of continuity in the NBA
quotes.excerpt: Anything can happen in professional sports. If somebody was in a coma for the last month, you wouldn't know.

text_blocks.speaker: Wosny Lambre
text_blocks.text: Anything can happen in professional sports. If somebody was in a coma for the last month, you wouldn't know what just happened in the NBA world. Kawhi is over here, we don't know where LeBron is going to be, Brendan Ingram and LaMelo are over here. Everybody is on the move.

text_blocks.speaker: Paul Pierce
text_blocks.text: They're the only ones with real continuity. Paul George is in Boston, Giannis is in Miami.

text_blocks.speaker: Wosny Lambre
text_blocks.text: Jaylen Brown in Philly. Like, what the fuck just happened in the last two weeks?

quotes.speaker: Danny Green
quotes.summary_phrase: Danny Green on Jaylen Brown's intelligence and personality
quotes.excerpt: I thought he was a humble kid. He's a grown man now, but he seemed like a humble dude.
quotes.quote: Instead of trying to reach and grab and pull every excuse or reason that they would do something not a smart move, just say it doesn't make sense. I don't get it. I thought he was a humble kid. I've met him, he's a grown man now, but he seemed like a humble dude. He is smart, he is a troll and he's funny. He has his Twitch, he has his stream and he's embracing it. But even when you hear him talk on stream, he doesn't sound like a very arrogant dude that thinks he knows it all.

quotes.speaker: Paul Pierce
quotes.summary_phrase: Paul Pierce calls the Jaylen Brown trade rumors lame
quotes.excerpt: This has got to be the lamest shit of an excuse for somebody to get traded.
quotes.quote: I've had a chance to digest this and listen to some of the things that have come out. This has got to be the lamest shit of an excuse for somebody to get traded.

quotes.speaker: Paul Pierce
quotes.summary_phrase: Paul Pierce defends the Celtics' status as a top-five team
quotes.excerpt: This is a top-five team. You forget what Luka did last year?

text_blocks.speaker: Paul Pierce
text_blocks.text: I think they're solidly out of the play-in, but they're not solidly out of the play-in. This is a top-five team.

text_blocks.speaker: Wosny Lambre
text_blocks.text: You forget what Luka did last year?

text_blocks.speaker: Paul Pierce
text_blocks.text: This is a top-five team. You're going to be worse defensively.

quotes.speaker: Danny Green
quotes.summary_phrase: Danny Green on the Jaylen Brown trade and the return value
quotes.excerpt: He's still a better player than what you got in return. The asset you got in return was not good enough.
quotes.quote: A lot of these reports that have come out, they don't really need to be said. Some of them sound very idiotic. They're just trying to make sense of it. Regardless of how you try, it doesn't make sense. I don't give a shit if he thinks he's the smartest guy in every room. He's still a better player than what you got in return. The asset you got in return was not good enough. It was unacceptable, damn near. And Paul George is a great player, but Jaylen Brown, all-NBA, could have been first team, all-NBA second team. He's 29 years old, not even 30, making the exact same amount of money.

quotes.speaker: Paul Pierce
quotes.summary_phrase: Paul Pierce on the absurdity of the Jaylen Brown trade excuses
quotes.excerpt: This has got to be the lamest shit of an excuse for somebody to get traded in all of all time.
quotes.quote: I've had a chance to digest this and listen to some of the things that have come out. This has got to be the lamest shit of an excuse for somebody to get traded in all of all time. When Luka got traded, I understood it. Oh, he doesn't play defense, he's out of shape. But when big names get traded, it's always something that comes out. You're the smartest guy in the room, he believes that, and his analytics didn't add up. But they won 50-plus games and were second in the East. You hear what I'm saying? These are the reasons he's supposedly left a sour taste in the organization's mouth to get traded? I can't believe this.

quotes.speaker: Paul Pierce
quotes.summary_phrase: Paul Pierce on Jaylen Brown's character and community impact
quotes.excerpt: This guy's been a model citizen. He's been a role model in the community.
quotes.quote: This guy's been a model citizen. He's been a role model in the community. These are things I know for a fact. I don't know anybody that said one bad thing about him. And because he comes out and has a chip on his shoulder from not making an Olympic team after being a finals NBA champion MVP, and then, you know, just dealing with shoe companies, he's coming out with his own brand. I mean, this is just ridiculous. I hope for success for Jaylen.

quotes.speaker: Wosny Lambre
quotes.summary_phrase: Wosny Lambre on the Celtics' management and Jayson Tatum
quotes.excerpt: Jaylen Brown has always felt like management looked at Tatum as the golden boy.
quotes.quote: I think management realized that they kind of came to the end of the road because of the nature of being together for a really long time. I think Jaylen Brown has always felt like management looked at Tatum as the golden boy, which is hard to say that's not true. I'll give you an example because the problem with the trade thing, they're not like being specific. At the games, Tatum's family is like front row. Jaylen Brown's family, 15 rows behind it. You know what I mean? And you guys know what that means politically within the organization. So if you're Jaylen Brown and you constantly feeling like I'm being looked at as not a 1A, just straight up I'm a B, and then this guy goes down and you come out and have the series, the season that you had for the team, and I think it's understandable that he would feel like, yo, there should be some level of adjustment in the pecking order, and I don't think Boston made that adjustment.

quotes.speaker: Danny Green
quotes.summary_phrase: Danny Green on the importance of respect in NBA relationships
quotes.excerpt: He deserved more respect than he was given. I think they definitely respected him.
quotes.quote: He deserved more respect than he was given. I think they definitely respected him, but they don't view him in the same light as Jayson. And he's always, he felt like he's always, and they knew that he was never going to be able to be outside of that shadow and they were like, it's time.

quotes.speaker: Wosny Lambre
quotes.summary_phrase: Wosny Lambre on the role of former players in front offices
quotes.excerpt: A lot of times they hire a player, ex-player to be GM. Boston doesn't have that guy.
quotes.quote: A lot of teams have a designated smooth shit over with the players guy. A lot of times they hire a player, ex-player to be GM. Like Sam Cassell like he over there, or like Jameer Nelson in Philly. A lot of teams have ex-players as the GM, the guy that's basically right underneath the president of basketball ops to be the smooth shit over guy. Boston doesn't have that guy. It's just Brad. And Brad is a basketball genius, but he might not be the best at communicating these delicate situations that might come up. And I think that hurt the relationship and the dynamic here into where where they get to a point where it's like, yo, this guy is like really unhappy with us and we don't think we can fix it.

quotes.speaker: Danny Green
quotes.summary_phrase: Danny Green on the importance of having a player-liaison in the front office
quotes.excerpt: You need a soothing transition or you need somebody to translate. However, you need a middle guy.
quotes.quote: All those things matter, man, when it comes to relationships anywhere, college, league, agent. You go with somebody you're comfortable with. You need somebody that's able to translate things. You need a soothing transition or you need somebody to translate. However, you need a middle guy that can be the glue. In the locker room, a lot of times, it takes some policing of itself for guys to get their egos in in order. If you don't have a couple guys in the locker room or a couple guys who set in front office to help them understand what's going on, it's going to be the way it is portrayed is not going to hit their ego the right way. It's going to be bad.

quotes.speaker: Wosny Lambre
quotes.summary_phrase: Wosny Lambre on Jaylen Brown's unhappiness with the Celtics
quotes.excerpt: It's been said that Jaylen Brown was like, bro, I don't need to be here no more either.
quotes.quote: At the end of the Philly series, Jaylen was like, I think we went away from the style that we used all year. Which everybody internally took it to mean we started shading things toward Jayson too much. As a guy who's just coming back and we had to establish this 56-win style. Like, how do you what do you think about expressing that publicly in a way that could easily be interpreted as like, I don't like that we're doing this Jayson shit again?

quotes.speaker: Paul Pierce
quotes.summary_phrase: Paul Pierce on the inevitability of player adjustments
quotes.excerpt: You're not going to play the same way that you played before Jason comes along.
quotes.quote: Jason's a superstar, too. You're going to adjust. You're not going to play the same way that you played before Jason comes along. But it just looks like it's throwing shade at Jason maybe. Like, you know what I'm saying? It just look like, you know, when he express it, it just make it seem like they're at odds or something or he didn't like the fact that they everything changed. But it has to. If I'm out the lineup, when we come back, we not playing that way. I don't care how many games we won. We going to play a y'all got to adjust because I'm out here, because I'm that type of player. You know what I'm saying? That's just the way it go.

quotes.speaker: Wosny Lambre
quotes.summary_phrase: Wosny Lambre on Andre Drummond joining the Knicks
quotes.excerpt: Andre Drummond is on his way to the New York Knicks. He'll step in for Mitchell Robinson.
quotes.quote: Speaking of defending champs, Andre Drummond is on his way to the New York Knicks. He'll step in for Mitchell Robinson who's headed to Boston. Drummond's also been making more corner threes lately, which could be useful as he backs up Karl-Anthony Towns.

quotes.speaker: Danny Green
quotes.summary_phrase: Danny Green on Andre Drummond as a replacement for Mitchell Robinson
quotes.excerpt: For what was left, I don't see much else better. Drummond is a solid backup.
quotes.quote: For what was left, I don't see much else better. Drummond is a solid backup. He rebounds well when he's motivated, when he's out there. When Joel was out, he played well. He also said knock down a corner three in the playoff. He played well from the playoffs. And it's again, it's spot minutes, limited minutes, like behind Cat, like it's a solid role. Then you also got Huk Porty.

quotes.speaker: Paul Pierce
quotes.summary_phrase: Paul Pierce on the Knicks' championship outlook
quotes.excerpt: Yeah, that'll be battling for a number one seed. Like when you win a championship, it just something.
quotes.quote: Yeah, that'll be battling for a number one seed. Like when you win a championship, it just something that does for your confidence. You get everybody coming back, you understand how to win. They'll they'll be better record wise if they stay healthy, 100%. I mean, they're more confident because it's just, you know, Danny you know, when you come back that next year, you step on the court like, you just feel like you can just press the button at any given moment, no lead is safe. Like, you know, you can be down 10, be like, all right guys, let's go, run, walk them down, win. And that's the type of confidence they're going to show next year if they don't have championship hangover.

quotes.speaker: Paul Pierce
quotes.summary_phrase: Paul Pierce on the Deandre Ayton trade
quotes.excerpt: Deandre Ayton dominating. The Lakers trade for Walker Kessler and immediately trade Ayton to the Washington Wizards.
quotes.quote: Deandre Ayton dominating. The Lakers trade for Walker Kessler and immediately trade Ayton to the Washington Wizards for Jaden Hardy and two Wizards second round picks.

quotes.speaker: Paul Pierce
quotes.summary_phrase: Paul Pierce on the Lakers' frontcourt rotation
quotes.excerpt: Walker Kessler is an upgrade over Deandre Ayton's starter minutes and now you have to get a guy.
quotes.quote: Walker Kessler is an upgrade over Deandre Ayton's starter minutes and now you have to get a guy that's going to be better than him, Jackson Hayes, in the bench minutes. Which I think, I think Jonas Valanciunas could give decent enough bench minutes.

quotes.speaker: Paul Pierce
quotes.summary_phrase: Paul Pierce on the Wizards' frontcourt mix
quotes.excerpt: I actually love it because you got a good mix of veterans and young guys.
quotes.quote: I actually love it because you got a good mix of veterans and young guys. You know what I'm saying? With the bench and Sar, you know, look at the work that AD has done over his career, probably pick up on some things from him and Ayton. So I really like it.

quotes.speaker: Paul Pierce
quotes.summary_phrase: Paul Pierce on the impact of LeBron James' documentary
quotes.excerpt: The non-LeBron major stuff is pretty much happening in terms of signings and trades.
quotes.quote: The non-LeBron major stuff is pretty much happening in terms of signings and trades. LeBron is basically the last domino that's falling and we wanted to kind of rank what we thought were the most impactful acquisitions that happened so far in this offseason, which is barely a freaking week old. But it's felt like a year, you know what I mean, with all the stuff that's happening.

quotes.excerpt: Not top six. You said top six. That's you're bugging.
